items.title: Class action claims women were raped and stalked at remote Fortescue mines
items.description: Andrew "Twiggy" Forrest's mining giant Fortescue has been slapped with a landmark class action alleging systemic sexual harassment, discrimination and toxic work sites.

items.title: Australia flags strengthening of social media ban
items.description: Australia will strengthen its social media ban for young people as a priority amid concerns the powers behind the world-first laws are not strong enough.

items.title: Hanson faces scrutiny as media landscape shifts around her
items.description: Parliament House has been Pauline's World lately but increased visibility comes with increased scrutiny and this week revealed that One Nation is not untouchable.

items.title: Live: At least 164 people killed after back-to-back earthquakes rock Venezuela
items.description: Venezuela's Acting President Delcy Rodríguez says at least 971 others have been confirmed injured after emergency services worked through the night to find those trapped under collapsed buildings. Follow live.

items.title: How Karl Stefanovic went from Today show glory to 'Joe Bogan'
items.description: Today show host Karl Stefanovic is reportedly leaving Channel Nine after a more than 20-year career at the network that was filled with highs and lows.

items.title: Former Liberal leader Matthew Guy denies assaulting MP Moira Deeming
items.description: Victorian MP Matthew Guy is considering legal advice to sue his party room colleague for defamation over the assault allegation, which is being investigated by police.

items.title: 'Nowhere near good enough': Eels coach fumes over error-ridden performance
items.description: Parramatta coach Jason Ryles has said his side's performance on Thursday night was not good enough to "beat a park football", going down 32-12 to the South Sydney Rabbitohs.

items.title: Live: Lions roar back in form with big win over Swans
items.description: The defending champions, Brisbane, make a statement with a big win over second-placed Sydney at the Gabba. Follow live.

items.title: Shark attack victim 'remembers the whole event in detail'
items.description: The 34-year-old's brother said she was awake, speaking with loved ones and her medical team and "remembers the whole event in detail".

items.title: Parent asks if 'warning signs' missed after Chinese language school closure
items.description: The shock closure of a Chinese language school after 17 years leaves parents and teachers with "unanswered questions" over the school's financial management.

items.title: Qantas axes Alice Springs-Melbourne route amid high cost, falling demand
items.description: Qantas has axed its direct Alice Springs-Melbourne route after "many decades", and will also restrict flights between Darwin and Singapore to the peak tourist season.

items.title: Laptop at the pub or office watch party: How Australian workers plan to watch the Socceroos
items.description: The countdown is on for Australia's World Cup match against Paraguay, and some football fans are preparing to happily put work on the backburner.

items.title: 'Some cracks' appearing in jobs market, even as unemployment rate dips
items.description: Australia's unemployment rate slipped to 4.4 per cent in May, down from 4.5 per cent in April, in seasonally adjusted terms.

items.title: 'Everybody is equal at the table': Inside the ACT's Circle Sentencing court
items.description: A pilot program allowing First Nations offenders to be sentenced by magistrates sitting alongside elders in the ACT Supreme Court secures funding for another three years.

items.title: Ghost nets transformed into art to highlight pollution's 'devastating' impact
items.description: Thousands of tonnes of ocean waste lands on Australia's shores every year. These Queenslanders have found a creative use for some of it.

items.title: Taking the plunge in chilly winter water to tackle loneliness
items.description: Young people are turning to local community groups to get out of their comfort zones, make real connections and boost their wellbeing.

items.title: When can gambling become an addiction? Here are the warning signs
items.description: Experts say the gambling industry is increasingly targeting women, and there are potential risks with a novelty bet.

items.title: Australians' tricks for dealing with heatwaves that Europeans yet to learn
items.description: Europe's record-breaking heatwave has highlighted its vulnerability to climate change. But countries could look to Australia's experience with scorching summers to learn valuable lessons.

items.title: Ex-AFL umpire to stand trial over alleged Brownlow fraud
items.description: Ex-AFL umpire Michael Pell, accused of leaking information on confidential Brownlow votes, has been ordered to stand trial.

items.title: Big battery boom means fewer transmission lines will be needed
items.description: Home batteries hit 600,000 as households play big role in energy transition, but building transmission projects remains "critical", according to the latest AEMO energy plan.

items.title: Sea bird sick with H5 avian flu landed by bodyboarders, too weak to fly to shore
items.description: A surfer who spotted the first bird in South Australia to test positive for H5N1 bird flu says the giant petrel looked fatigued and distressed before it was retrieved by wildlife rescuers.

items.title: Antic's 'dangerous' comments on vaccinations condemned
items.description: South Australian Liberal senator Alex Antic has been roundly condemned over comments he made about vaccinations after avian influenza was found on Australia's southern coast.

items.title: Traffic cones on statues and a sea of orange: The traditions taking over the World Cup
items.description: Every four years, the World Cup provides the perfect backdrop for fans to showcase their culture's traditional football rituals in front of millions.

items.title: Teals Allegra Spender and Zali Steggall form new political party
items.description: The teal independents have confirmed they are forming a new political party, Community Strong Australia, but are yet to convince crossbench colleagues to join what they call a "responsible alternative" to the major parties.

items.title: 'ISIS bride' barred from Australia issued permit to return
items.description: Australia's home affairs minister approves the return of a woman who has links to Islamic State and has been in a Syrian refugee camp, saying the government plans to have her under high-level surveillance.
